en.greeting: Hi! Today you'll learn to sum up texts and conversations for other people, and to explain Indonesian notices, menus and words like mudik in English. Let's go step by step.

steps.title: What a summary is
steps.text: At A2 you passed on short messages and the key facts of a notice. Now let's sum up longer texts and whole conversations for someone else.
steps.body: A **summary** (ringkasan) is the short version for a colleague, a friend or your boss. Give the **main point** first, then the **2–3 key facts** they need: often what, when, where, and what they have to do. Use **your own words** and keep it much **shorter** than the original. Leave out greetings, examples and small details, and never add facts or your own opinion. First ask: **who is it for, and what do they need?**

steps.title: Summing up texts and talks
steps.text: Read these aloud. Look at how each summary starts.
steps.body: A **text** you can still read (an email, an article, a notice): **says** + present. A **conversation** that's over: **said / told** and the verb **one step back**, like in the reported speech lesson (*is → was, can → could, will → would*).

examples.en: Basically, the email says the lift is broken until Friday.
examples.id: Intinya, email itu bilang liftnya rusak sampai Jumat.

examples.en: In short, the article says remote work is good for parents, but it can be lonely.
examples.id: Singkatnya, artikel itu bilang kerja jarak jauh bagus untuk orang tua, tapi bisa bikin kesepian.

examples.en: Sari told me she was sick, so she couldn't finish the report.
examples.id: Sari bilang ke aku dia sakit, jadi dia tidak bisa menyelesaikan laporannya.

examples.en: Pak Hasan said the new design was great, but it was too expensive.
examples.id: Pak Hasan bilang desain barunya bagus sekali, tapi terlalu mahal.

examples.en: The main point is that the meeting is now on Thursday.
examples.id: Intinya, rapatnya sekarang hari Kamis.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Yesterday Budi from the Bandung office called you. Mr Lee wasn't there.

question.prompt: Budi said: 'Our new printer doesn't work. The technician can only come on Thursday, so we can't print the reports before Friday. Sorry!' Which is the best summary for Mr Lee?
options: Budi said the technician could come on Thursday.
Budi said the new printer didn't work, so the reports were ready on Thursday.
Budi said their new printer didn't work, so they couldn't print the reports before Friday.
question.explanation: The best summary has the **main point** (the printer doesn't work) and the **key fact** for Mr Lee (no reports before Friday), with said + one step back. The technician is only a detail, and *ready on Thursday* changes the facts.

steps.title: What's missing?
steps.text: Tom was on leave, and he has 200 emails. He asks what HR said.

question.prompt: HR's email: 'From next month the office opens at 7.30. Everyone can choose to work from 7.30 to 4.30 or from 9 to 6. Please tell your manager your choice by Friday.' Sari's summary: 'From next month we can work from 7.30 to 4.30 or from 9 to 6.' What did she leave out?
options: The new working times.
What Tom has to do by Friday.
When the change starts.
question.explanation: The summary has the times and *from next month*, but not the action: **tell your manager your choice by Friday**. What the listener has to do, and by when, is almost always a key fact.

steps.title: Explaining an Indonesian text
steps.text: Tom, Emma and Mr Lee can't read Indonesian. When they ask 'What does it say?', you explain.
steps.body: Don't translate every word. Ask: **what does it mean for them?** What can or can't they do, when, and how much? Skip *Dengan hormat* and *Atas perhatiannya*. Rules: **dilarang** → **You can't…** or **No + -ing**; **wajib** → **You have to…**; **mohon / harap** → **Please…**. A **di-** verb sounds best with a person: *Pagar dikunci* → ***They lock** the gate*. On a **menu**, keep the dish name and explain it. Prices: **Rp25.000** → **Rp25,000** in English.

pairs.en: No smoking. / You can't smoke here.
They lock the gate at 10 p.m.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Tom just moved into your kos and can't read the notice in the kitchen.

question.prompt: The notice: 'Sampah dibuang setiap hari Selasa dan Jumat sebelum jam 7 pagi. Dilarang memasak di dalam kamar.' Which explanation is best for Tom?
options: The garbage throws every Tuesday and Friday before 7. Forbidden cooking in room.
Put your rubbish out on Tuesdays and Fridays before 7 a.m. You can't cook in your room.
Put your rubbish out every day before 7 a.m. You can cook in your room.
question.explanation: It gives both rules in natural English: the **di-** verb becomes an instruction for Tom (*Put your rubbish out*), and **dilarang** → **You can't**. The first is word for word and unclear (garbage can't throw!); the third changes the facts. (*rubbish* is British; Americans say *trash* or *garbage*.)

steps.title: Words with no English word
steps.text: Tom asks: 'What's mudik?' There's no English word for it, so keep the word and explain it.
steps.body: Use one of three patterns, then add one or two key facts. **It's a kind of** + a thing: *Angkringan is a kind of food cart.* **It's when** + a person + a verb: *Mudik is when people travel to their hometown for Lebaran.* **It's like** + a thing from their country + **but** + the difference: *A kos is like a shared house, but you rent only one room.* Don't forget **a**: *It's kind of sweet* means 'agak manis'. And don't translate names: *nasi kucing* isn't 'cat rice'!

steps.title: Indonesian words, explained
steps.text: Here's how you might explain some everyday words to Emma.
steps.body: Keep the Indonesian word, use a pattern, then add a fact or two. Two short sentences are clearer than one long one.

examples.en: Gotong royong is when neighbours work together for free, for example to clean the street.
examples.id: Gotong royong: tetangga bekerja bersama tanpa dibayar, misalnya membersihkan jalan.

examples.en: Angkringan is a kind of food cart. It sells cheap snacks and hot drinks until late at night.
examples.id: Angkringan: gerobak makanan yang menjual camilan murah dan minuman panas sampai larut malam.

examples.en: Nasi kucing is a very small portion of rice with sambal and a little fish.
examples.id: Nasi kucing: nasi porsi kecil dengan sambal dan sedikit ikan.

examples.en: Lebaran is Eid, the big holiday at the end of Ramadan.
examples.id: Lebaran adalah Idulfitri, hari raya besar di akhir Ramadan.

examples.en: A kos is like a shared house, but the owner often lives there and makes the rules.
examples.id: Kos mirip rumah bersama, tapi pemiliknya sering tinggal di sana dan membuat aturan.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Emma's neighbour invited her to an arisan, and she asks you what it is.

question.prompt: Which explanation of arisan is best for Emma?
options: Arisan is a kind of party.
It's a regular meeting of friends or neighbours. Everyone pays the same amount into a pot, and each time one person wins all the money.
It's like a bank, but for women. You save money there and get interest.
question.explanation: It says what an arisan is (a regular meeting) and adds the key facts: everyone pays, and each time one person wins the pot. *A kind of party* is too vague: Emma still knows nothing about the money. And an arisan isn't a bank: there's no interest.

steps.title: Build the explanation
steps.text: Tom sees 'ojek' in an app and asks what it is. Use the It's like …, but … pattern.

question.prompt: Arrange the words to explain ojek.
question.solution: It's like a taxi, but on a motorbike.
question.explanation: **It's like** + a familiar thing (a taxi) + **but** + the difference (on a motorbike). Then add a fact: *You sit on the back, and you can book it on an app.*

steps.title: Cheat sheet
steps.text: Here's everything on one page. Keep it for later.

tips: Ask first: **who is it for, and what do they need to know or do?** Main point first, then the key facts.
Don't copy or translate word by word: *Forbidden cooking in room* ✗ → **You can't cook in your room.**
**It's a kind of** needs **a**; **It's when** needs a person + a verb (*It's when people go…*).

examples.en: In short, Pak Hasan said the client wanted a lower price.
examples.id: Singkatnya, Pak Hasan bilang kliennya ingin harga yang lebih murah.

examples.en: Gotong royong is when neighbours work together for free.
examples.id: Gotong royong: tetangga bekerja bersama tanpa dibayar.

id.greeting: Hai! Hari ini kamu belajar meringkas teks dan percakapan untuk orang lain, serta menjelaskan pengumuman, menu dan kata-kata seperti mudik dalam bahasa Inggris. Yuk, pelan-pelan saja.

steps.title: Apa itu ringkasan
steps.text: Di A2 kamu menyampaikan pesan pendek dan fakta penting dari sebuah pengumuman. Sekarang kita ringkas teks yang lebih panjang dan percakapan utuh untuk orang lain.
steps.body: **Ringkasan** (summary) adalah versi pendek untuk orang yang tidak ada di sana. Sampaikan **intinya** (main point) dulu, lalu **2–3 fakta penting** (key facts) yang dia perlukan: sering apa, kapan, di mana, dan apa yang harus dia lakukan. Pakai **kata-katamu sendiri** dan buat jauh **lebih pendek** dari aslinya. Lewati salam, contoh dan detail kecil, dan jangan menambah fakta atau pendapatmu. Tanya dulu: **untuk siapa, dan apa yang dia perlukan?**

steps.title: Meringkas teks dan obrolan
steps.text: Baca keras-keras. Perhatikan bagaimana setiap ringkasan dimulai.
steps.body: **Teks** yang masih bisa dibaca (email, artikel, pengumuman): **says** + bentuk sekarang. **Percakapan** yang sudah lewat: **said / told** dan kata kerjanya **mundur satu langkah**, seperti di pelajaran reported speech (*is → was, can → could, will → would*).

examples.en: Basically, the email says the lift is broken until Friday.
examples.id: Intinya, email itu bilang liftnya rusak sampai Jumat.

examples.en: In short, the article says remote work is good for parents, but it can be lonely.
examples.id: Singkatnya, artikel itu bilang kerja jarak jauh bagus untuk orang tua, tapi bisa bikin kesepian.

examples.en: Sari told me she was sick, so she couldn't finish the report.
examples.id: Sari bilang ke aku dia sakit, jadi dia tidak bisa menyelesaikan laporannya.

examples.en: Pak Hasan said the new design was great, but it was too expensive.
examples.id: Pak Hasan bilang desain barunya bagus sekali, tapi terlalu mahal.

examples.en: The main point is that the meeting is now on Thursday.
examples.id: Intinya, rapatnya sekarang hari Kamis.

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Kemarin Budi dari kantor Bandung meneleponmu. Mr Lee sedang tidak ada.

question.prompt: Budi bilang: 'Our new printer doesn't work. The technician can only come on Thursday, so we can't print the reports before Friday. Sorry!' Mana ringkasan terbaik untuk Mr Lee?
options: Budi said the technician could come on Thursday.
Budi said the new printer didn't work, so the reports were ready on Thursday.
Budi said their new printer didn't work, so they couldn't print the reports before Friday.
question.explanation: Ringkasan terbaik memuat **intinya** (printernya tidak berfungsi) dan **fakta penting** untuk Mr Lee (laporan tidak bisa dicetak sebelum Jumat), dengan said + mundur satu langkah. Teknisinya hanya detail, dan *ready on Thursday* mengubah faktanya.

steps.title: Apa yang terlewat?
steps.text: Tom baru kembali dari cuti dan punya 200 email. Dia bertanya apa kata HR.

question.prompt: Email HR: 'From next month the office opens at 7.30. Everyone can choose to work from 7.30 to 4.30 or from 9 to 6. Please tell your manager your choice by Friday.' Ringkasan Sari: 'From next month we can work from 7.30 to 4.30 or from 9 to 6.' Apa yang terlewat?
options: The new working times.
What Tom has to do by Friday.
When the change starts.
question.explanation: Ringkasannya memuat jam kerja dan *from next month*, tapi tidak memuat tindakannya: **tell your manager your choice by Friday**. Apa yang harus dilakukan pendengar, dan kapan batasnya, hampir selalu fakta penting.
displayOptions: Hal yang harus Tom lakukan paling lambat Jumat.

steps.title: Menjelaskan teks berbahasa Indonesia
steps.text: Tom, Emma dan Mr Lee tidak bisa membaca bahasa Indonesia. Saat mereka bertanya 'What does it say?', kamu yang menjelaskan.
steps.body: Jangan terjemahkan setiap kata. Tanyakan: **apa artinya bagi mereka?** Apa yang boleh atau tidak boleh, kapan, dan berapa? Lewati *Dengan hormat* dan *Atas perhatiannya*. Aturan: **dilarang** → **You can't…** atau **No + -ing**; **wajib** → **You have to…**; **mohon / harap** → **Please…**. Kata kerja **di-** paling enak dengan orangnya: *Pagar dikunci* → ***They lock** the gate*. Di **menu**, nama makanan tetap, lalu jelaskan. Harga: **Rp25.000** → **Rp25,000** dalam bahasa Inggris.

pairs.en: No smoking. / You can't smoke here.
They lock the gate at 10 p.m.

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Tom baru pindah ke kosmu dan tidak bisa membaca pengumuman di dapur.

question.prompt: Pengumumannya: 'Sampah dibuang setiap hari Selasa dan Jumat sebelum jam 7 pagi. Dilarang memasak di dalam kamar.' Penjelasan mana yang terbaik untuk Tom?
options: The garbage throws every Tuesday and Friday before 7. Forbidden cooking in room.
Put your rubbish out on Tuesdays and Fridays before 7 a.m. You can't cook in your room.
Put your rubbish out every day before 7 a.m. You can cook in your room.
question.explanation: Kedua aturannya tersampaikan dalam bahasa Inggris yang wajar: kata kerja **di-** menjadi petunjuk untuk Tom (*Put your rubbish out*), dan **dilarang** → **You can't**. Pilihan pertama kata per kata dan tidak jelas (sampah tidak bisa membuang!); pilihan ketiga mengubah faktanya. (*rubbish* itu British; orang Amerika bilang *trash* atau *garbage*.)

steps.title: Kata yang tidak ada padanannya
steps.text: Tom bertanya: 'What's mudik?' Tidak ada satu kata bahasa Inggris untuk itu, jadi pertahankan katanya dan jelaskan.
steps.body: Pakai salah satu dari tiga pola, lalu tambahkan satu atau dua fakta penting. **It's a kind of** + benda (= semacam): *Angkringan is a kind of food cart.* **It's when** + orang + kata kerja (= saat/ketika): *Mudik is when people travel to their hometown for Lebaran.* **It's like** + sesuatu dari negara mereka + **but** + bedanya: *A kos is like a shared house, but you rent only one room.* Jangan lupa **a**: *It's kind of sweet* artinya 'agak manis'. Dan jangan terjemahkan nama: *nasi kucing* bukan 'cat rice'!

steps.title: Kata-kata Indonesia, dijelaskan
steps.text: Begini caranya menjelaskan beberapa kata sehari-hari ke Emma.
steps.body: Pertahankan kata Indonesianya, pakai salah satu pola, lalu tambahkan satu atau dua fakta. Dua kalimat pendek lebih jelas daripada satu kalimat panjang.

examples.en: Nasi kucing is a very small portion of rice with sambal and a little fish.
examples.id: Nasi kucing: nasi porsi kecil dengan sambal dan sedikit ikan.

examples.en: Lebaran is Eid, the big holiday at the end of Ramadan.
examples.id: Lebaran adalah Idulfitri, hari raya besar di akhir Ramadan.

examples.en: A kos is like a shared house, but the owner often lives there and makes the rules.
examples.id: Kos mirip rumah bersama, tapi pemiliknya sering tinggal di sana dan membuat aturan.

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Tetangga Emma mengajaknya ikut arisan, dan Emma bertanya kepadamu apa itu.

question.prompt: Penjelasan arisan mana yang terbaik untuk Emma?
options: Arisan is a kind of party.
It's a regular meeting of friends or neighbours. Everyone pays the same amount into a pot, and each time one person wins all the money.
It's like a bank, but for women. You save money there and get interest.
question.explanation: Penjelasan ini menyebut apa itu arisan (pertemuan rutin) dan menambahkan fakta pentingnya: semua orang menyetor, dan setiap kali satu orang mendapat seluruh uangnya (*the pot*). *A kind of party* terlalu kabur: Emma tetap tidak tahu soal uangnya. Dan arisan bukan bank: tidak ada bunganya.

steps.title: Susun penjelasannya
steps.text: Tom melihat 'ojek' di sebuah aplikasi dan bertanya apa itu. Pakai pola It's like …, but … .

question.solution: It's like a taxi, but on a motorbike.
question.explanation: **It's like** + sesuatu yang Tom kenal (taksi) + **but** + bedanya (naik motor). Lalu tambahkan fakta: *You sit on the back, and you can book it on an app.*
